In the Oldest Stories, Medusa Was Born a Gorgon
In Hesiod's Theogony, Medusa is born a Gorgon, the only mortal of three sisters. The beautiful woman whose hair became snakes comes later, from Ovid. A Spell Spoken to the Heart
Spell 30B speaks directly to the heart. In an old translation, it begins, "My heart my mother." On this heart scarab, the museum identifies ten lines as Spell 30B. Why Does Anubis Have a Canine Head?
Why a canine head? One idea, noted by the Met, starts in the cemeteries: a watchful canine could be imagined as a guardian of the dead. It is an interpretation, not proof. Heart and Feather in Balance
People often say the heart had to be lighter than the feather. Here, the heart is not shown lighter. The two sides hang in balance.
